BACONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qov.oh S. ZOLI OPINION NO. JUN 10 202} RIZA Accounting Officer Park Developers Inc. acctngpdi@gmail.com Dear MS. RIZA: This refers to your electronic mail dated 01 April 2024 wherein you are requesting for guidance on the following queries, to wit: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. What if the small-scale business do not have a business permit, where can a complaint be filed especially of the municipality gives them favor? Can the municipal office be subject of a complaint since it tolerates the small- scale businesses to operate without a mayor's permit? Can we file a complaint against the municipality because of tolerance of the operation of small-scale businesses without a mayor's permit? Where can we file a complaint against the mayor of the municipality? Through the DILG or the Ombudmsman? In what department can we file a complaint? At the outset, we would like to highlight that all businesses, unless exempt, are required to secure a mayor's permit or business permit from the city or municipality where they are located, to ensure that the standards are met and that, the business complies with the specific requirements and guidelines. Accordingly, Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), as amended, the mayor of the municipality or city has the authority to issue license and permits pursuant to the general welfare clause. Congruently, businesses that operate without the required mayor's permit or whose permit has expired, are operating illegally and thus, may be subject to liability, potential sanctions including fines, penalties, and business closure. In this regard, a small-scale business operating without mayor's permit or business permit can be reported to the municipality through its business permits and licensing office. As to the 2nd to 5th queries, considering that the matter is interrelated, we deem it proper to tackle the issues in one discussion. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Evidently, considering that a mayor's permit is necessary to enable a business to operate legally within a certain locality, allowing businesses to operate without complying with the required Mayor's Permit, is contrary to law. Consequently, such act denotes a flagrant and culpable unwillingness to perform a duty and those responsible will be opening themselves to a possible administrative case for gross neglect of duty or dereliction of duty, as may be warranted by evidence, which are grounds for disciplinary action under Section 60(c) of the LGC. Correspondingly, an administrative case may be filed before the sangguniang panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President, as provided under Sec. 61 of the LGC. Notwithstanding, we would like to highlight that this opinion should not be used against any officials as the purpose of which is only to address your concem / query. Let it be noted that this Department has no jurisdiction to determine whether or not an official is criminally or administratively liable as the same should be threshed out with the proper authority. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BYT AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: R R. LLAMAS or External, Legal and Legislative Affairs rsecret SELLA/JVRULLLS-LRALLD/rjki Page 2 of 2
